intro: Lesson 44: Group 7: the halogens and displacement. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Complete the displacement results grid for Cl₂, Br₂ and I₂ with KCl, KBr and KI (3), explain the pattern (1), and write one balanced equation (2).
questions.a: Cl₂ reacts with KBr and KI; Br₂ reacts with KI only; I₂ none (3); reactivity decreases down the group (1); e.g. Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂ (2)
questions.model: Teacher fills the chlorine row: 'No reaction with KCl; orange with KBr; brown with KI.'

questions.q: Fluorine is above chlorine. Predict its reaction with sodium chloride solution in principle and its reactivity.
questions.a: Would displace chlorine (1) because it is the most reactive halogen (1)

questions.q: Why is hydrogen chloride gas not the same as chlorine gas in properties?
questions.a: It is a compound with different bonding and properties from the element Cl₂.

questions.q: Write the balanced equation for bromine + sodium iodide.
questions.model: Bromine above iodine, so it displaces. Br₂ + NaI → NaBr + I₂; two iodides needed for I₂, so 2NaI and 2NaBr.

questions.q: Predict the state and colour of astatine at room temperature.
Why does iodine not react with potassium chloride?
questions.a: Iodine is less reactive than chlorine
